title: printf and scanf
summary: printf prints with a format string where each % specifier stands for a value - %d, %f, %c, %s, %zu, %x - with optional width and precision. scanf reads input with the same kind of specifiers, into variables whose addresses you pass with &, and returns how many values it managed to read, which you should always check.

cards.q: Which specifier prints a double with exactly 3 decimals?
cards.a:
%.3f

The precision goes after a dot.

scanf needs n's address to store into it

Without `&`, scanf gets n's (garbage) value instead of where n lives, so it cannot store the number.

cards.q: What does scanf return if the user types "abc" for %d?
cards.a:
0: it read no values

Always check the return value.

cards.q: Which scanf specifier reads a double?
cards.a:
%lf

In scanf, %f is for float and %lf for double. In printf, %f prints both.
